title: harden findings file
description: Schema for .harden/findings.json (verified findings) and .harden/candidates.json (stage-1 detections, same shape, verified=false). scripts/validate_findings.py implements every rule below by hand (stdlib only) and adds the checks JSON Schema cannot express: unique ids, file and line existence and spelling (repo mode), base_sha and commit existence, nit cap, approvals record, verifier_id distinct from pass_ids (detection DT-27). Sources: final-report-and-impact G204-F02/F03/F04/F06/F07/F08/F12/F19/F21, skill-design T31-F10/F11, industry-review-guidelines T02-F03/F13, standards T01-F01, reviewer-independence G201-F05/F11/F12.

base_sha.description: Commit the pass started from (git rev-parse HEAD at preflight). File and line locations refer to this commit.

generated.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp when the file was written.

tool_versions.description: Pinned version of every tool whose output is cited as evidence, e.g. {"eslint": "9.12.0", "ruff": "0.6.9"}. Deltas are valid only under identical pinned tool and config (G204-F12).

kind.description: tool = tool output (command, rule id, SARIF path); test = test id that fails before / passes after; repro = command plus observed output; source = file:line code-path trace; git = commit or history evidence; doc = documentation. In-repo comments and docs are claims to verify, not proof (G201-F05).

ref.description: Where the evidence can be re-checked: command line, test id, file:line, SARIF path, commit sha.

detail.description: Short excerpt of the output or trace.

kind.description: project-config = the project's own tool configuration sets the threshold; skill-default = a default from this skill's references (cite the rule id); vendor-default = the tool's shipped default.

ref.description: Where the threshold can be re-checked: config file path and key, skill rule id, or the tool's documentation.

id.description: Unique within the file, e.g. H-001.

rule_ref.description: Skill rule id (e.g. DC-03) or a project tool rule as project:<tool>/<rule> (e.g. project:eslint/no-unused-vars).

file.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes, at base_sha.

class.description: structural: must not change observable behaviour, tests unmodified. behavioural: intentionally changes behaviour; own commit, a test demonstrating it, explicit approval. report-only: never edited.

tier.description: T0 auto-apply (mechanically proven, structural only); T1 apply after category approval; T2 owner judgement: report only with --interactive or while the run profile's auto_apply.owner_judgement is false; with it true, the owner-judgement lane of an autonomous run may apply a T2 item, which keeps tier T2 as the mark of its origin and carries a review object (user-policy-autonomy U01-F06).

severity.description: Small ordinal scale anchored to the written rubric; never a decimal score (G204-F01).

severity_criterion.description: The rubric line this severity meets, quoted or cited (G204-F02). Required unless severity is nit.

confidence.description: Evidence ladder, highest first; never the model's self-reported confidence (G204-F03).

verified.description: True only after a fresh-context verification confirmed the finding against file:line or executable evidence (T31-F10).

commit.description: Commit that applied the fix (required when status is applied).

cwe.description: CWE id when one applies, e.g. CWE-561 (standards T01-F01).

quality_characteristic.description: Optional. ISO/IEC 5055 characteristic the finding is filed under, next to its CWE id (standards T01-F01: CWE-1306 Reliability, 1307 Maintainability, 1308 Security, 1309 Efficiency). Vocabulary only; never a compliance claim.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity used to match this finding across runs (mirrors SARIF partialFingerprints).

blocking.description: Optional. True only for a verified correctness, security or data-integrity defect, or a behaviour change introduced by the pass (G204-F21, T02-F03). Absent means non-blocking.

unblock_condition.description: Optional. What exactly unblocks a blocking finding (G204-F21).

conditions.description: Optional second axis: preconditions needed to trigger the problem (G204-F02).

seen_in_passes.description: Optional. Number of independent detection passes whose candidates were clustered into this finding (detection DT-23). Orders triage, never filters it. validate_findings.py warns when it disagrees with the number of distinct pass_ids.

pass_ids.description: Optional. Ids of the detection passes (subagents) that produced this cluster (detection DT-21, DT-23).

exclusion_class.description: Optional. False-positive exclusion class a rejected candidate falls under (detection DT-33, classes 1-7), e.g. 'DT-33(2) generated or vendored'. Only meaningful with status rejected; copied to the SARIF suppression.

threshold_source.description: Optional. Where a numeric threshold behind the finding comes from (prioritization PZ-16, PZ-17): the project's own config, a skill default, or a tool vendor's default.

verifier_id.description: Optional. Id of the fresh-context verifier that admitted or rejected the finding (detection DT-27). Must differ from every id in pass_ids; validate_findings.py makes that an error on established statuses.

baseline_state.description: Optional. State against the baseline run, copied to SARIF result.baselineState (reporting RP-19; SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.27.24).

review.description: Why this applied change waits for the owner's review before merge (reporting RP-07, Applied, review before merge; user-policy-autonomy U01-F06, U01-F11 to U01-F13). kinds, in the report's order: breaking-api (the commit subject has '!' before the colon and a BREAKING CHANGE footer), additive-api, contract-source (a .sol or .vy file changed: the fix takes effect only when the owner redeploys), money-path, owner-judgement (applied by the owner-judgement lane; required on an approved, applied, partial or reverted T2 finding), behavioural, whole-repo-format. option: the choice the lane made where two behaviours were valid (prioritization, Owner-judgement lane step 3), 'direct' when there was none; alternatives names the behaviours left to the owner and is required unless option is 'direct'. Required on an applied or partial T2 or behavioural finding, and on one whose commit changes a contract source.

allOf.$comment: Reported-like statuses need verification and at least one evidence item with a ref.
Applied and partial findings name their commit (partial: reporting RP-16, eval-v2-calibration E02-F02).
T0 is reserved for structural changes.

T2 is report only unless the owner-judgement lane of an autonomous run applied it (user-policy-autonomy U01-F06): an approved, applied, partial or reverted T2 finding carries a review object whose kinds hold owner-judgement.
Class report-only is never approved, applied, partial or reverted.
An applied or partial behavioural change carries a test demonstrating the new behaviour.
An applied or partial T2 or behavioural finding carries a review object for the report's Applied, review before merge (reporting RP-07; user-policy-autonomy U01-F13).
Critical/high findings presented as established need proof (G204-F04). validate_findings.py downgrades this to a warning for deferred/blocked and skips candidate/rejected.
Blocking findings presented as established need the same proof as critical/high (G204-F04).
Confidence rungs must be backed by the matching evidence kind (G204-F03).
Every severity except nit cites its rubric criterion (G204-F02); rejected candidates are exempt.
Blocking is narrow and states what unblocks it (G204-F21).
